The interval statement is accurate: the original inclusive-rule processes are constant on intervals [0,e1), [e1,e2), ..., [es,1], so switches are included at the left edge of the next segment.
Title, author, date, and DOI agree with the journal record.

The first r3/r4 definitions cite switch mechanics and exact arithmetic; the later duplicate r3/r4 definitions cite outcomes and scope. This makes the claims' citations ambiguous/invalid. notes.filename: Computational Modelling of Trust and Social Relationships.md
verified: 3000 cycles, per-agent turns, FM forage/social choice, new-versus-existing alter probabilities, all four alter-selection strategies, directed trust, trust waning/floor, tercile outcome definitions, and global-defection limitation are supported by the cited model sections.
MaxCR=10, MinCR=0, MaxTrust=100 are the parameters specified for the logarithmic trust-increase experiments.

The stated finding that strong-tie and staged strategies better reproduce SBH layers than medium/weak strategies is supported by the results; scope is appropriately limited to model fit, not platform intervention validation.
Date, DOI, authors, and title are consistent with JASSS metadata.
notes.bibliography: The note says three imported reference identifiers remain unresolved and that equal counts do not establish title mapping; adequate caveat. It contains 41 items, the same count as the source list, but unresolved titles mean individual mapping is still unverified.
exact_issues: The model summary still omits the defining experimental comparison of linear versus logarithmic trust waning. The paper tests a 2x2 combination of linear/log trust increase and linear/log waning; the note mentions only linear versus logarithmic trust increase, then leaves waning as generic 'trust wanes.' Add both waning variants and say the log-increase/linear-decrease configuration best fit the SBH distribution (Sections 4.5-4.10), so the described mechanism/results are not misleadingly incomplete.

The note describes the response and trust update only generically. Clarify that a cooperative response increments trust and a defection decrements trust according to the selected increase/decrease function, and that waning follows each social turn in the model-control sequence (Section 3.23). The note's current 'then trust wanes' is directionally correct but under-specifies the update variant just noted.
notes.limitations: Source bibliography item mappings remain unresolved but caveat is explicit. The outstanding failure is model-method coverage, not evidence that the stated model claims are false.
